title: Sahel salt caravan
summary: For many centuries long camel caravans have carried slabs of salt out of the Sahara, from mines such as Taoudenni to Timbuktu and, in Niger, from Bilma to Agadez. The journey takes weeks over dunes and between wells, and the caravan must share water, loads and trust.
howToPlay: Lead a salt caravan along the map from the mine to the market.
Tap a choice, or press its number, to decide how your caravan loads, rests and trades.
When the well-keeper asks you to share the slabs, pick the answer you think is right.
Water, salt and goodwill change as you choose; your ending gives one to three stars.
rules: The caravan passes five places on the map and has three possible endings.
Careful, fair and patient choices earn wisdom points; rushing and cheating earn none.
Wandering lost, driving a lame camel, pushing at the well, hiding cracks and a wrong share cannot be undone and cost the best ending.
The sharing puzzle is answered once; a wrong answer starts a dispute.
Three stars need water, salt and goodwill and none of those missteps.
heritageNote: Salt caravans, known as azalai, have crossed the Sahara for centuries, led by Tuareg and other desert families who know the wells and the stars. Slabs from the Taoudenni mines still travel to Timbuktu, and in Niger a caravan carries salt from Bilma to Agadez. This is an original tale of one such crossing.
